facts.title: The company in numbers
facts.peLoss: Not applicable: it made a loss

help.marketCap: What the company is worth on the stock market: one share's price times all its shares.
help.pe: How many years of earnings you pay for the share: its price divided by earnings per share.
help.dividendYield: What the company pays out in dividends in a year, as a % of the share price.
help.eps: Last year's profit divided by the number of shares, in the currency of its accounts.
help.beta: How much it moves compared with the market: 1 is the same as the market; above 1, it moves more.
help.ter: What the fund charges you each year to run it, as a % of what you have invested.

window.title: Markets open now
window.note: Times in your device's time zone. Europe: Madrid, Frankfurt and Paris open at the same time.

ideas.title: Lists to practise with
ideas.intro: Lists with a clear rule, built from real data, so you can practise analysis. Pick a company, open it and ask yourself why it's on the list.
ideas.teaser: Lists with a clear rule to practise analysis.
ideas.notAdvice: This is not a recommendation: these are lists for you to practise analysis.
ideas.empty: No data yet. Check back in a while.
ideas.followed: Added to your favourites to study it
ideas.followError: Couldn't save it. Please try again.

drops.title: Biggest fallers in the last session
drops.short2: Large companies with the biggest drop
drops.criterion: Shares from the major indices (S&P 500, IBEX 35, Euro Stoxx 50, Nikkei 225…) with the biggest drop in their last session.
drops.warning: A drop is not an opportunity on its own. First find out why it fell.

dividend.title: High dividend
dividend.criterion: Shares with a dividend yield above 4%, both the expected one and the last 12 months'. Largest first.
dividend.warning: A very high dividend can be a warning sign. Check whether the company earns enough to pay it.

lowPe.title: Low P/E for its sector
lowPe.criterion: Profitable shares (P/E above 0) with a P/E below the median of their sector. Largest first.

ibex.title: Large IBEX 35 companies
ibex.short2: The most valuable on the market
ibex.criterion: The 10 IBEX 35 companies worth the most on the stock market (by market cap).

etf.title: Broad index ETFs
etf.criterion: Exchange-traded funds that track broad indices: the whole world, the S&P 500, Europe or emerging markets.

chart.lastCandle: Market closed: the last candle is from {date}.
chart.error: Couldn't load the chart. We'll keep trying.
chart.unavailable: Yahoo Finance has no {iv} for this asset. Try another button.

info.notAdvice: Data to understand the asset, not a recommendation.

status.hoursFx: Hours: from Sunday 23:00 to Friday 23:00 (Madrid time)
status.hoursFutures: Hours: almost 24 hours, Sunday to Friday, with a daily break from {range} (Madrid time)

help.change: How much the price has gone up or down since the previous session closed.
help.change_crypto: How much it has gone up or down since midnight UTC, the reference Yahoo uses for crypto (it never closes).
help.dayRange: Today's lowest and highest price. The dot shows where it is now.
help.range52: The lowest and highest price of the last year. It shows whether it's now close to one of its extremes.
help.volume: How many shares have changed hands today. High volume means a lot of interest.
help.volume_etf: How many fund units have changed hands today on this exchange.
help.volume_crypto: How much money has been traded in the last 24 hours, across many platforms.
help.volume_commodity: How many futures contracts have been bought and sold today.
help.volume_index: What has been traded today in the index's companies, added up.
help.avgVolume: What trades on a normal day (average of the last 3 months). Compare it with today's.
help.prevClose: The price at which the previous session closed: the reference for today's change.
help.prevClose_crypto: The price at midnight UTC: the reference for the day's change.
help.marketCap: What the company is worth on the stock market: the price of one share times all the shares.
help.marketCap_crypto: What all the coins in circulation are worth at the current price.
help.pe: How many years of current earnings you pay for the company: the share price divided by earnings per share.
help.dividendYield: What the company pays out in dividends in a year, as a % of the share price.
help.dividendYield_etf: What the fund pays out each year, as a % of its price. Accumulating funds don't pay out: they reinvest.
help.eps: Last year's profit divided by the number of shares, in the currency of its accounts.
help.beta: How much it moves compared with the market: 1 is the same as the market; above 1, it moves more.
help.ter: What the fund charges you each year to manage it, as a % of what you have invested.
help.totalAssets: How much money everyone who owns the fund has invested in it in total.
help.family: The company that creates and manages the fund.
help.category: The fund's type of investment according to Yahoo: for example, large US companies.
help.inception: Since when the fund has existed. A longer history shows how it behaved in crises.
help.circulating: How many coins already exist and can be bought or sold.
help.allTimeHigh: The highest price it has ever had.
help.sector: The broad area of the economy the company works in.
help.industry: Its specific activity within the sector.
help.employees: People working full time at the company.
help.country_listing: The country of the exchange where it is bought and sold.
help.exchange: The market where it is bought and sold. It opens and closes at set hours.
help.currency: The currency it trades in. If it isn't the euro, the exchange rate also changes what you gain or lose.
help.currency_index: An index has no currency: it is measured in points and can't be bought directly.
help.currency_fx: An exchange rate tells you how many units of one currency one unit of the other costs.
help.delay: Some exchanges only give prices for free with a few minutes of delay.
help.contract: The futures market where the contract trades: the price is that of the contract that expires first.
